replies:
You don't have a resume on file here yet. The one step that starts this: paste your resume (or paste the Experience, Skills, Education and Projects sections). I'll read it and save each entry as draft facts.

While you paste, use this quick checklist I apply for Junior Software Engineer roles — the gaps I look for and that often hurt early-career candidates:

1. Clear header and target
 - One-line title (e.g., "Junior Software Engineer") and contact email. No objective fluff.

2. Concise summary (optional)
 - If you include one, one sentence naming the role you want and your top stack or strength.
3. Experience entries framed as achievements
 - 1–4 bullets per job/project showing what you built or improved, the tech used, and measurable impact where possible (load, performance, users, time saved, bugs reduced).
 - Use past tense for prior roles, present for current.

4. Projects section with demos/links
 - At least 2 projects showing end-to-end work (frontend + backend or deployed API). For each: what you built, tech, and one result or lesson. Include GitHub/Live links.

5. Skills section, structured
 - Separate Languages, Frameworks, Tools, Databases, DevOps/Testing. Keep to truth and to what you can speak to in an interview.
6. Technical depth signals
 - One or two bullets showing testing, CI/CD, deployment, performance tuning, or database design — whatever you actually did.

7. Quantified impact and context
 - Replace duties with metrics: "Cut API response time 40% by indexing and query refactor" beats "Worked on APIs."

8. Education and relevant coursework (if early-career)
 - Degree, school, grad year. Include relevant classes or honors only if you lack professional experience.

9. Formatting for ATS and readability
 - Single page if <5 years experience, clear section headings, consistent bullets, no images or columns that break parsers.
10. Keywords from target postings
 - Truthfully include required terms you can back up in an interview (e.g., React, TypeScript, REST, SQL, unit tests).

Paste your resume now and I will:
- read and save each entry as draft facts,
- summarize in 2–3 lines what I read (latest role, top skills, education),
- give 2–3 specific changes to make it stronger for Junior SRE/Software Engineer roles,
- offer to search for matching jobs after that.

One question: do you want your contact info anonymized when I save the resume (yes/no)?
